assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of Sr clocks with record accuracy and stability, are a textbook case of a measurement method that opens new observation: fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, relativistic redshift measured across millimetres, and a route to redefining the second and to searches for varying constants and dark matter. It is experimentally concrete and field-opening.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003) and made early Sr demonstrations; Ye's group drove the performance to the best published levels and the many-body clock work. The supplied credit lists exactly these two, a clean two-person configuration. Priority versus other groups (e.g., Hg lattice clocks, Lemonde) and the Hall/Hansch comb context are minor.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs reproduce 1e-18-level performance, comparisons over fibre links exist, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Timely, and the field has moved well beyond proof of principle.
uncertainties: Whether a prize should also recognize Pierre Lemonde or ion-clock groups is not settled by the supplied credit.
I cannot independently verify exact current uncertainty records and priority dates from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry with atoms and molecules has turned inertial forces and gravity into precisely measurable quantities: gravimeters, gyroscopes, tests of the equivalence principle and measurements of G and alpha. It is a measurement technique with real instruments and broad uptake, and relies on laser cooling and coherent manipulation I know well.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated atom interferometry with a nanofabricated grating; Mlynek and colleagues showed the Young double-slit with atoms (with Carnal); Kasevich and Chu realized the light-pulse interferometer for precision gravimetry. Chu already received the 1997 prize for related cooling work, and the supplied list omits Chu, so the three-person set is plausible but credit is contested between grating-based and light-pulse approaches.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the lab and increasingly in field instruments; the interpretation is stable. Applications to fundamental tests continue to develop, so recognition is timely though some headline goals (gravitational waves, equivalence principle at 1e-15) are not yet reached.
uncertainties: Which strand (grating versus light-pulse) is decisive is unresolved.
Overlap with Chu's earlier prize may complicate the configuration.
Exact first-demonstration dates are from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single nitrogen-vacancy centres provide optical readout and coherent control of a single spin at room temperature, a genuinely new sensing platform for magnetic fields, temperature and electric fields at the nanoscale, with applications from condensed matter to biology. This matches my interest in new measurement capabilities and in impact beyond physics.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko achieved the first optical detection and coherent control of single NV spins (1997, 2004); Lukin's group developed the quantum-sensing and nanoscale magnetometry demonstrations and register ideas. The supplied three-name set fits a coherent configuration, though the nanoscale magnetometry contributions of Awschalom, Hanson and Yacoby groups are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation worldwide; many instruments and early commercial products. Application sensitivity and robustness in biological settings are still developing, which tempers claims of maturity.
uncertainties: Credit for sensing demonstrations is spread over several groups beyond the supplied names.
I cannot verify claims about commercial impact from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed-vacuum injection beyond the shot-noise limit in gravitational-wave interferometers is a concrete quantum-enhanced measurement now in routine operation at GEO600, LIGO and Virgo. It links a proposal to a demonstrated, practical improvement in detector sensitivity and is a strong example of quantum optics enabling a new observation of nature.
assessment.attribution: Caves proposed squeezed-state injection in 1981; Schnabel's group led long-term demonstrations including GEO600 and frequency-dependent squeezing; Mavalvala's group contributed to LIGO's squeezing implementation and quantum noise work. Kimble's earlier squeezing and frequency-dependent squeezing proposals are also credited in the list, so selecting three involves excluding an important contributor.
assessment.maturity: Mature in implementation: squeezing is installed in the large detectors and its benefit is measured. Fundamental squeezing physics was recognized in part through other prizes and the 2017 award, which could reduce prize room.
uncertainties: Whether the 2017 gravitational-wave prize makes this redundant to the committee.
Allocation between Kimble, Schnabel and Mavalvala is ambiguous.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-matter quantum interfaces, namely the proposal for quantum state transfer between photons and atomic ensembles and the experimental realization of quantum-network elements, underpin quantum memories, repeaters and networks. I know from rare-earth memory work how hard efficient storage with long coherence is, and I value that this was both proposed and demonstrated in several platforms.
assessment.attribution: Cirac, Zoller, Kimble and Mabuchi described the quantum internet concept and the interface protocols; Kimble's group built cavity QED and ensemble experiments, with Lukin, Polzik, Lvovsky and others contributing substantially. The three-name set is defensible but excludes several decisive experimentalists, and the work spans several distinct platforms.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: elementary links and memories are demonstrated, but efficient, scalable networks and repeaters remain a goal, and the applied relevance is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The discovery is a compound of theory proposals and diverse experiments, so decisive credit is hard to isolate.
Rare-earth and ensemble memory contributions are not in the credited names, and I should be careful of my own field bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics realized strong coupling of a superconducting qubit to a single microwave photon and became the standard architecture for superconducting quantum processors, dispersive readout and quantum-limited amplification. It has clear experimental consequences and large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues wrote the theory proposal (2004), Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in the same year. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration, though Devoret and others contributed adjacent prize-recognized work and the 2025 prize recognized macroscopic circuit quantum tunnelling.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced, but overlap with the recent circuit-quantum prize may reduce timeliness.
uncertainties: Overlap with the most recent prize for superconducting circuits.
Division of credit with Devoret, Martinis and Nakamura groups is not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical coherence tomography is an interferometric imaging technique that opened non-invasive micrometre-scale cross-sectional imaging, with huge clinical impact especially in ophthalmology. It is a clear case of an instrument whose use reaches far beyond physics, which matters to me from my own work on imaging, though its physics novelty (low-coherence interferometry) is modest.
assessment.attribution: The 1991 Science paper by Huang, Swanson, Fujimoto and colleagues established OCT; earlier low-coherence reflectometry work (Fercher, Takada, Youngquist) complicates priority. The supplied three-name set is reasonable but the priority issue is real.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with widespread clinical adoption and Fourier-domain improvements confirming it. Whether it counts as physics for this prize versus medicine or engineering is a concern.
uncertainties: Priority relative to Fercher's group and others.
Fit with the physics prize criteria.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled trapped atoms and ions implement quantum gates and simulation: the Cirac-Zoller ion-trap proposal and Blatt's demonstration of entangling gates and algorithms in ion strings gave the first working quantum processors. It is a solid experimental-plus-theory achievement with direct influence on quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller proposed the gate (1995) and the Innsbruck group under Blatt realized it, alongside Wineland's NIST group, who already received a prize in 2012 for related control. The name list also includes Bloch, whose optical-lattice work appears in a separate entry. A three-name set from the supplied four is plausible but ties to other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with trapped-ion processors still among the most precise. Recognition may be partially covered by the 2012 prize, and the broader quantum computing area is crowded.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Wineland and Haroche prize.
Choice of three out of four names and overlap with other candidates containing Cirac, Zoller and Bloch.
